scope: Static source/artifact review only; no assembly, scanner, fixture, command, or subprocess was invoked.
axes: host probes and descendant processes cannot escape the measurement boundary
receipts bind the executed tool and runner
assessment: The delivered isolated-clone C1 assembler and measurement runner have strong static fixture/root checks and preserve payloads as JSON data, but the selected scanner is imported/executed as Python. Tool-path trust and process isolation remain open. The separate replay wrapper runs round-21 harnesses, not the new round-22 C1 measurement runner.

findings.title: C1 executes the selected scanner with caller privileges
findings.exploit_path: The new C1 measure.py accepts --tool, resolves it, verifies only that the resolved target is a regular file, and passes it to a child wrapper that imports the file and calls exec_module. There is no repository/path allowlist or no-network/low-privilege sandbox in the direct CLI. A malicious or unintended external or in-repository Python file can run at import. A modified candidate scanner could also execute untrusted transcript code; PyCF_ONLY_AST in the current scanner is source evidence for that file, not an enforcement boundary for future candidate bytes.
evidence: .ufo/worktrees/r22-oracle/.ufo/waves/round-22/oracle/measure.py:655-668 starts the child with inherited environment and only an address-space/time limit
.ufo/worktrees/r22-oracle/.ufo/waves/round-22/w1/reports/OracleHarness.md:21-27 describes the direct --tool interface and AST-only payload intent
tools/mado-tripwire.py:2101-2114 uses PyCF_ONLY_AST for the current source
findings.impact: If the selected source is not trusted, it can read private files/secrets or initiate host/network actions. If a candidate scanner executes JSONL code instead of parsing it, the fixtures can trigger the same effects; resource/time caps do not prevent that.
findings.smallest_remediation: Restrict --tool to explicitly approved scanner path(s) and independently sealed hashes; verify the invocation path before resolution so symlinks cannot bypass policy. For adversarial candidate bytes or to guarantee payload non-execution, require a separately authorized unprivileged, no-network, read-only fixture sandbox.

findings.title: Replay oracle mode retains the round-21 manifest path risk
findings.exploit_path: The main-lane replay.py oracle mode selects .ufo/waves/round-21/oracle/measure.py. That reference runner joins case.fixture to ROOT without containment checks; tools/mado-tripwire.py permits ~/.omp/agent/sessions. A traversal fixture plus a rewritten colocated expected.sha256 can therefore redirect a later round-21 replay if those old manifest files are writable. This is not a path escape in the new isolated-clone C1 runner: it constrains cases to inputs/<case-id>.jsonl, rejects symlink components, checks exact population, and revalidates before and after.
evidence: .ufo/waves/round-21/oracle/measure.py:49-60 uses ROOT / case['fixture'] without containment validation
.ufo/worktrees/r22-oracle/.ufo/waves/round-22/oracle/measure.py:109-125,503-540 confines and inventories R22 fixture paths
findings.impact: A tampered historical replay manifest could cause private session JSONL to be read/classified; the current new C1 fixture path check prevents the same straightforward traversal through its expected case.fixture.
findings.smallest_remediation: Do not use replay.py --mode oracle as the R22 C1 entry path. If historical replay remains authorized, confine its fixture paths and reject symlinks/escape exactly as the new C1 runner does; externally pin its expected manifest.

findings.title: A detached scanner descendant escapes process-group cleanup
findings.exploit_path: The updated R22 runner kills the scanner's process group on timeout and normal completion, but arbitrary selected Python can spawn a descendant in a new session/process group before returning. That descendant is outside the scanner PGID; killpg on the original group can report it empty while the detached process continues. The outer replay wrapper has the same process-group limitation.
evidence: .ufo/worktrees/r22-oracle/.ufo/waves/round-22/oracle/measure.py:656-712 kills only the scanner process group
findings.impact: A deliberately detached child can retain the caller's privileges after a timeout or successful receipt and continue file or host-probe actions.
findings.smallest_remediation: For an adversarial scanner, use an OS process-tree boundary such as a separately authorized cgroup/PID namespace sandbox that prevents descendants from escaping; process-group cleanup alone is not containment.

findings.title: Replay records tool drift without making it a failure
findings.exploit_path: The main-lane replay wrapper records tool digests before and after but returns the underlying round-21 runner status without comparing the digests, and it records the runner digest only before launch. A changed tool can therefore accompany exit 0/1. The new R22 C1 measure runner is stronger: it revalidates tool, runner, producer, population, and source inputs and returns 2 on post-run integrity failure.
findings.impact: Replay process status alone is not proof that the reported result used stable bytes; readers must not treat a receipt with differing before/after hashes as a pass.
findings.smallest_remediation: Make replay exit 2 on any tool-digest mismatch and verify an independently sealed runner digest before and after launch.

static_safety_controls: The isolated-clone assembler reads strictly parsed, digest-sealed source/proposal artifacts and writes only beside its own __file__; it serializes proposal cells to JSONL and does not execute them.

The new C1 runner starts each scanner in its own session and kills/reports that group on timeout and normal completion; this cleans same-group descendants but cannot contain a selected module that deliberately starts a separate session.
The current mado-tripwire.py parses eval source using PyCF_ONLY_AST, but this is not a sandbox for a future selected scanner.
The audit-contract CLI is artifact-only by contract, but no new C2 audit implementation was present at inspection.
